questions.question: Is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ already in Jordan normal form?
options: No, because the diagonal entries are equal.
Yes, it is a single Jordan block.
Only if the determinant is zero.
No, because it is not diagonal.

questions.question: If a Jordan normal form has diagonal entries $2,2,3$, what are its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity?
options: 2 and 3 each once only.

questions.question: Why is Jordan normal form useful for defective matrices?
options: It still gives a structured form using generalized eigenvectors.
It turns defective matrices into diagonalizable matrices.
It avoids any change of basis.
It removes all eigenvalues from the matrix.

questions.question: Does the equation $J_A=P^{-1}AP$ mean A and $J_A$ represent the same linear operator in different bases?
options: Only if P is the identity matrix.
Yes, they are similar matrices.
No, they have unrelated eigenvalues.
No, $J_A$ is obtained by row reduction.

questions.question: For $J=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix}$, what are the Jordan block sizes?
options: One block of size 2 for 5 and one block of size 1 for 2.
One block of size 3 for 2.
Three blocks of size 1 only.
One block of size 2 for 2 and one block of size 1 for 5.

questions.question: When is Jordan normal form exactly diagonal rather than merely almost diagonal?
options: When there is exactly one eigenvalue.
When the matrix is singular.
When all Jordan blocks have size 1.
When every block has size at least 2.

questions.question: Which statement about the existence of a Jordan normal form is correct?
options: It exists over $\mathbb{C}$ for every square matrix, not always over $\mathbb{R}$.
It exists only for matrices that are diagonalizable over $\mathbb{C}$.
It exists over $\mathbb{R}$, with real entries, for every real square matrix.
It exists only for matrices whose eigenvalues are all distinct.

questions.question: A $4\times4$ matrix has a single eigenvalue $\lambda$ with $\operatorname{am}(\lambda)=4$ and $\operatorname{gm}(\lambda)=2$. Which block sizes can its Jordan normal form have?
options: Either $2+2$ or $3+1$
Only $2+2$
Only one block of size $4$

questions.question: The Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$ consists of two $1\times1$ blocks and one $2\times2$ block, all for the eigenvalue $2$. What are $\operatorname{am}(2)$ and $\operatorname{gm}(2)$?
options: $\operatorname{am}(2)=4$, $\operatorname{gm}(2)=3$
$\operatorname{am}(2)=3$, $\operatorname{gm}(2)=4$
$\operatorname{am}(2)=4$, $\operatorname{gm}(2)=1$
$\operatorname{am}(2)=4$, $\operatorname{gm}(2)=4$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$. Which matrix is a Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2+\sqrt{2}&0\\0&2-\sqrt{2}\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: A $3\times3$ matrix $\boldsymbol{A}$ has the Jordan normal form $\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix}$. Which statement is correct?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}5&0&0\\0&2&1\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$ is also a Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&5&1\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$ is also a Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix}$ is also a Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$
The given matrix is the only Jordan normal form of $\boldsymbol{A}$
